answer: Each agent may join cheaply, but it cannot immediately claim valuable work: rewards unlock only after a random bond is held through several rounds and the agent completes tasks assigned across independent peers. A sybil cluster must therefore lock capital in every fake identity and keep each one active long enough to build a credible thread of completion history. Peer rotation makes it harder to fake consensus; the prism is that one identity can sit on the ledge of eligibility, but only costly, sustained participation moves it forward.
